anf_compare.notes: Translated from the PG 74 Greek; no published English version was used for wording.

bible_refs.note: Direct quotation: εἴτε γὰρ ἐξέστημεν, θεῷ· εἴτε σωφρονοῦμεν, ὑμῖν.
Paraphrase of ηὐχόμην γὰρ ἀνάθεμα εἶναι αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ἀπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὑπὲρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου, introduced with φησίν; 'those of my own blood' = Paul's 'kinsmen according to the flesh'.
Near quotation of the list υἱοθεσία … ἐπαγγελίαι and ἐξ ὧν ὁ Χριστὸς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα; Cyril writes αὐτῶν for ὧν and adds αὐτός.
αὐτῶν οἱ πατέρες, καὶ τὰ ἄλλα: Cyril picks up ὧν οἱ πατέρες and abbreviates the rest.
Lemma: Οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι ἐκπέπτωκεν ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ — exact.
πατὴρ ἔσται πολλῶν summarises LXX ἔσῃ πατὴρ πλήθους ἐθνῶν (17:4) and πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε (17:5); same numbering in LXX and Hebrew.

πληθύνων πληθυνῶ τὸ σπέρμα σου matches LXX Genesis 22:17; the ending ὡσεὶ τὰ ἄστρα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τῷ πλήθει matches Exodus 32:13 LXX (and Hebrews 11:12). Cyril blends the promise texts; cited by the opening wording.
στοιχοῦσι τοῖς ἴχνεσι τῆς ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ πίστεως — Paul's phrase, introduced with κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον.
Direct quotation of both verses, with φησί inserted.
ὡς ἐν Ἰσαὰκ τὸ ἐξ Ἁβραὰμ λελόγισται σπέρμα echoes ἐν Ἰσαὰκ κληθήσεταί σοι σπέρμα (9:7, from Genesis 21:12) and λογίζεται εἰς σπέρμα (9:8).
Direct quotation: κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον ἐλεύσομαι καὶ ἔσται τῇ Σάρρᾳ υἱός (Paul from Genesis 18:10, 14).
οὐ τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκὸς … εἰς τέκνα Θεοῦ and τὰ ἐκ τῆς ἐπαγγελίας follow Romans 9:8.
Lemma begins: Οὐ μόνον δέ, ἀλλὰ καὶ Ῥεβέκκα ἐξ ἑνὸς … — continues at the head of u08-rem-early.

choices.why: οὐκ ἀνικάνως ἔχουσαν: litotes ('not insufficiently able'), rendered 'quite able'.
βραβευτὴς τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν οἰκειότητος: 'arbiter/steward of their closeness to him'; 'steward' chosen for plain sense.

choices.english: would not, simply and in every case, be counted
choices.why: οὐ … πάντη τε καὶ πάντως: Cyril limits rather than flatly denies — not every child of the flesh is automatically a child of God; rendered 'would not, simply and in every case, be counted'.

choices.term: ἐφ' ἑαυτοῖς τὴν ἐπὶ τῷδε δόξαν
choices.why: ἐφ' ἑαυτοῖς τὴν ἐπὶ τῷδε δόξαν: 'the honor (glory) of this'; 'honor' chosen because δόξα here means standing or repute, not divine glory.

choices.english: who had not known from ancient times
choices.why: τῶν οὐ πάλαι διεγνωκότων: 'who had not known from ancient times', that is, latecomers to the knowledge of God.

pass_a_gloss: …of all to go toward destruction (ὄλεθρον). This was of one netting (σαγηνεύοντος) the Jews into ready-obedience (εὐπείθειαν), and beating off (ἀποκρουομένου) the slanders (συκοφαντίας) of the senseless (ἀσυνέτων). For some of the Jews supposed the divine (θεσπέσιον) Paul, as become struck-senseless (ἀπόπληκτον), to oppose (ἀντιφέρεσθαι) the laws through Moses; for this reason to those who believed he writes saying 'For whether we were beside ourselves (ἐξέστημεν), to God; whether we are sober-minded (σωφρονοῦμεν), to you.' So I would choose, and very eagerly, he says, in order that I might save (ἀνασώσαιμι) those from (my) blood, to be anathema (ἀνάθεμα) from Christ. And he adds on, as showing the cause of his grief (λύπης) over them not insufficiently holding toward being able to work in him such a disposition (διάθεσιν), lest he seem to say something hard and harsh-sounding (ἀπηχές), giving as gift his own (life) as exchange (ἀντάλλαγμα) for the life of others. For first, he says, they are Israelites; theirs the adoption (υἱοθεσία) and the glory and the covenants (διαθῆκαι) and the law-giving (νομοθεσία) and the worship (λατρεία) and the promises (ἐπαγγελίαι); and from them according to flesh even Christ himself. But if they were some of those not long having known the One being by nature (φύσει) and truly God, if the law through Moses had not become for them umpire/steward (βραβευτής) of the closeness (οἰκειότητος) toward him, if they had not grown from the root (ῥίζης) of the holy fathers and been set as heirs of their fame (εὐκλείας), if they had not first practised the ways of worship toward God and been enriched with the hopes of the promise, one would have made the grief over them more moderate. But since theirs the fathers, and the rest; and the affairs all but going for them from a fair wind (ἐξ οὐρίας), they have fallen out into an unexpected end and missed (διημαρτήκασι) the hope; how is what befell the wretched not truly all-terrible? 'Not as though the word of God has fallen out (ἐκπέπτωκεν).' Exact the saying; for least of all, he says, has it lied (διεψεῦσθαι), that is, can the word of God fall away from the truth; for the God of all things confessedly promised (ἐπήγγελται) to Abraham in the beginnings that he will be father of many; and again 'Multiplying I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude.' It was necessary therefore that Abraham be shown father not of those from Israel only; for one nation was the one appearing from him, but countless those over all the earth, which also have been set as children to Abraham, if indeed they are from promise and walk in line (στοιχοῦσι) with the footprints (ἴχνεσι) of his faith in foreskin (ἀκροβυστίᾳ), according to what is written; for as blessed Paul himself somewhere says 'Not through law the promise to Abraham that he be heir of the world, but through righteousness (δικαιοσύνης) of faith; for if those from law are heirs, he says, faith has been emptied (κεκένωται) and the promise abolished (κατήργηται).' When therefore as in Isaac the seed from Abraham has been reckoned (λελόγισται), that is according to undertaking (ὑπόσχεσιν), for of promise is this word 'According to this season I will come and to Sarah there will be a son,' it would be clear surely that not the children of the flesh would be counted (καταλογισθεῖεν) entirely and by all means into children of God, but rather those from the promise, that is those through faith, would have upon themselves the glory (δόξαν) on this. 'And not only, but also Rebecca from one…'
pass_b_english: …for all, to go to destruction. This was the act of one who was drawing the Jews into ready obedience as with a net, and beating back the slanders of the foolish. For some of the Jews thought that the inspired Paul had, as it were, lost his mind and was setting himself against the laws given through Moses. That is why he writes to those who had believed, “For if we are beside ourselves, it is for God; if we are in our right mind, it is for you” (2 Corinthians 5:13).

So, he says, I for my part would very gladly choose to be accursed from Christ, if only I could save those of my own blood (Romans 9:3). Then he adds, as if to show that the cause of his grief over them is quite able to work such a disposition in him, so that he might not seem to have said something harsh and jarring in offering his own life in exchange for the life of others: For first, he says, they are Israelites; theirs are the adoption and the glory and the covenants and the giving of the law and the worship and the promises; and from them, according to the flesh, comes Christ himself (Romans 9:4–5).

Now if they had been among those who had not known from ancient times the One who is God by nature and in truth, if the law given through Moses had not become for them the steward of their closeness to him, if they had not sprung from the root of the holy fathers and been made heirs of their good name, if they had not been the first to practice the ways of worshiping God and had not grown rich in the hopes of the promise, then one would have grieved over them more moderately. But since “theirs are the fathers,” and the rest (Romans 9:5), and since, when their affairs were all but running before a fair wind, they have fallen into an end no one expected and have missed their hope, how is what has befallen these wretched people not truly dreadful?

“But it is not as though the word of God has failed” (Romans 9:6). The statement is exact. For he says that the word of God has by no means proved false, that is, that it cannot fall away from the truth. For the God of all, as everyone agrees, promised Abraham at the beginning that he would be the father of many (Genesis 17:4–5), and again, “I will surely multiply your offspring like the stars of heaven in number” (Genesis 22:17).

Abraham, then, had to be shown to be the father not of those from Israel alone. For the nation that came from him was one, but the nations throughout the whole earth are past counting, and they too have been reckoned as Abraham’s children, if indeed they are of the promise and “walk in the footsteps of the faith” he had “in uncircumcision” (Romans 4:12), as it is written. For as blessed Paul himself says somewhere, “The promise to Abraham that he would be heir of the world did not come through the law, but through the righteousness of faith. For if those who are of the law are heirs,” he says, “faith has been emptied and the promise made void” (Romans 4:13–14).

Since, then, the offspring of Abraham has been reckoned as being in Isaac, that is, according to promise (Romans 9:7–8), for this is the word of promise, “About this time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son” (Romans 9:9), it would surely be plain that the children of the flesh would not, simply and in every case, be counted as children of God (Romans 9:8). Rather, it is the children of the promise, that is, those who come through faith, who would have that honor for themselves.
“And not only so, but also Rebecca, by one…” (Romans 9:10).
source_text:
πάντων χωρῆσαι πρὸς ὄλεθρον. τοῦτο δὲ ἦν σαγηνεύοντος μὲν τοὺς Ἰουδαίους εἰς
εὐπείθειαν, ἀποκρουομένου δὲ τὰς τῶν ἀσυνέτων συκοφαντίας· ᾤοντο γὰρ τῶν
Ἰουδαίων τινὲς οἷον ἀπόπληκτον γεγονότα τὸν θεσπέσιον Παῦλον, τοῖς διὰ Μωυσέως
ἀντιφέρεσθαι νόμοις· ταύτῃτοι τοῖς πιστεύσασιν ἐπιστέλλει λέγων "Εἴτε γὰρ ἐξέστημεν,
Θεῷ, εἴτε σωφρονοῦμεν, ὑμῖν." οὐκοῦν ἑλοίμην ἂν ἔγωγε καὶ μάλα προθύμως, φησὶν,
ἵνα τοὺς ἐξ αἵματος ἀνασώσαιμι, ἀνάθεμα εἶναι ἀπὸ Χριστοῦ· προσεπάγει δὲ, ὥσπερ τῆς
ἐπ' αὐτοῖς λύπης τὴν αἰτίαν οὐκ ἀνικάνως ἔχουσαν ἀποφαίνων εἴς γε τὸ δύνασθαι
τοιαύτην αὐτῷ τὴν διάθεσιν ἐνεργάζεσθαι, ἵνα μή τι δοκοίη σκληρόν τε καὶ ἀπηχὲς
εἰπεῖν, τῆς ἑτέρων ζωῆς ἀντάλλαγμα τὴν ἑαυτοῦ δωρούμενος· πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ, φησὶν,
εἰσὶν Ἰσραηλῖται, αὐτῶν ἡ υἱοθεσία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ αἱ διαθῆκαι καὶ ἡ νομοθεσία καὶ ἡ
λατρεία καὶ αἱ ἐπαγγελίαι· ἐξ αὐτῶν δὲ τὸ κατὰ σάρκα καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Χριστός· ἀλλ' εἰ μέν
τινες ἦσαν τῶν οὐ πάλαι διεγνωκότων τὸν φύσει τε καὶ ἀληθῶς ὄντα Θεὸν, εἰ μὴ νόμος
αὐτοῖς ὁ διὰ Μωυσέως γέγονε βραβευτὴς τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν 225 οἰκειότητος, εἰ μὴ τῆς τῶν
ἁγίων πατέρων ἐξέφυσαν ῥίζης καὶ τῆς ἐκείνων εὐκλείας τέθεινται κληρονόμοι, εἰ μὴ
πρῶτοι τοὺς τῆς εἰς Θεὸν λατρείας μεμελετήκασι τρόπους, καὶ τὰς τῆς ἐπαγγελίας
πεπλουτήκασιν ἐλπίδας, μετριωτέραν ἄν τις τὴν ἐπ' αὐτοῖς ἐποιήσατο λύπην. ἐπειδὴ δὲ
αὐτῶν οἱ πατέρες, καὶ τὰ ἄλλα· μόνον δὲ οὐχὶ καὶ ἐξ οὐρίας αὐτοῖς τῶν πραγμάτων
ἰόντων, εἰς ἀδόκητον ἐκπεπτώκασι τέλος καὶ διημαρτήκασι τῆς ἐλπίδος· πῶς οὐ
πάνδεινον ἀληθῶς τὸ τοῖς ἀθλίοις συμβεβηκός; Οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι ἐκπέπτωκεν ὁ λόγος τοῦ
Θεοῦ.
Ἀκριβὴς ὁ λόγος· ἥκιστα γὰρ διεψεῦσθαί φησιν, ἤγουν δύνασθαι τῆς ἀληθείας
διαπεσεῖν τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ λόγον· ἐπήγγελται μὲν γὰρ ὁμολογουμένως τῷ Ἁβραὰμ ἐν
ἀρχαῖς ὁ τῶν ὅλων Θεὸς, ὅτι πατὴρ ἔσται πολλῶν· καὶ πάλιν "Πληθύνων πληθυνῶ τὸ
σπέρμα σου ὡσεὶ τὰ ἄστρα τοῦ "οὐρανοῦ τῷ πλήθει·" ἔδει τοίνυν οὐχὶ μόνων τῶν ἐξ
Ἰσραὴλ ἀναδειχθῆναι πατέρα τὸν Ἁβραάμ· ἔθνος γὰρ ἦν ἓν τὸ ἐξ αὐτοῦ πεφηνὸς, μυρία
δὲ ὅσα κατὰ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν, ἃ καὶ εἰς τέκνα τέθεινται τῷ Ἁβραὰμ, εἴπερ εἰσὶν ἐξ
ἐπαγγελίας, καὶ "στοιχοῦσι τοῖς ἴχνεσι τῆς ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ "πίστεως" αὐτοῦ, κατὰ τὸ
γεγραμμένον· ὡς γὰρ αὐτός που φησὶν ὁ μακάριος Παῦλος "Οὐ διὰ νόμου ἡ ἐπαγγελία
τῷ "̔Αβραὰμ εἰς τὸ κληρονόμον αὐτὸν εἶναι κόσμου, ἀλλὰ διὰ "δικαιοσύνης πίστεως· εἰ
γὰρ οἱ ἐκ νόμου κληρονόμοι, φησὶ, "κεκένωται ἡ πίστις καὶ κατήργηται ἡ ἐπαγγελία."
ὅτε τοίνυν ὡς ἐν Ἰσαὰκ τὸ ἐξ Ἁβραὰμ λελόγισται σπέρμα, τουτέστιν καθ' ὑπόσχεσιν,
ἐπαγγελίας γὰρ ὁ λόγος οὗτος Κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦτον ἐλεύσομαι καὶ ἔσται τῇ Σάῤῥᾳ
υἱὸς, δῆλον ἂν εἴη δήπουθεν ὅτι οὐ τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκὸς καταλογισθεῖεν ἂν πάντη τε
καὶ πάντως εἰς τέκνα Θεοῦ, ἔχοιεν δ' ἂν 226 μᾶλλον ἐφ' ἑαυτοῖς τὴν ἐπὶ τῷδε δόξαν τὰ
ἐκ τῆς ἐπαγγελίας, τουτέστιν τὰ διὰ πίστεως. Οὐ μόνον δὲ, ἀλλὰ καὶ Ῥεβέκκα ἐξ ἑνὸς
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Staged translation checked clause by clause; it joins cleanly to the end of u07-rem-close, and Scripture IDs (2 Corinthians 5:13; Romans 9:3, 9:4–5, 9:5, 9:6, 9:7–9, 9:10, 4:12, 4:13–14; Genesis 17:4–5, 22:17) are right. Fixed in tr7.json: (1) 'those who had not long known the One who is God' for τῶν οὐ πάλαι διεγνωκότων can read as the opposite sense, now 'who had not known from ancient times'; (2) δῆλον ἂν εἴη was 'it must surely be plain', now 'it would surely be plain' to keep the potential mood; (3) 'he adds more' trimmed to 'he adds'; (4) British spellings honour/practise/worshipping changed to honor/practice/worshiping to match this work's rows (Savior, honored); (5) the row had 19 one-sentence paragraphs, regrouped into 7 paragraphs by thought, matching the adjacent u07 rows; no words added or dropped in regrouping. Two translator notes added.
Copy-text: PG 74; Fragmenta in Romanos via Khazarzar (Fragmenta in sancti Pauli epistulam ad Romanos.pdf), PG columns 224–226.

The row opens mid-sentence: the end of u07-rem-close reads καὶ εἷς ὑπὲρ, so πάντων χωρῆσαι πρὸς ὄλεθρον completes 'one for all to go to destruction'. The English keeps the cut with an ellipsis and adds no missing words.
The row ends mid-lemma at Ῥεβέκκα ἐξ ἑνὸς; κοίτην ἔχουσα Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν stands at the head of u08-rem-early. Romans 9:10 is cited at both edges.
Inline PG column numbers 225 and 226 are print markers and are left out of the English.
σαγηνεύοντος: literally 'catching in a dragnet' (σαγήνη); rendered 'drawing … as with a net' to keep Cyril's image.
ἀπόπληκτον: 'struck senseless, out of his mind'; it answers ἐξέστημεν in 2 Corinthians 5:13.
οὐκ ἀνικάνως ἔχουσαν: litotes ('not insufficiently able'), rendered 'quite able'.
βραβευτὴς τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν οἰκειότητος: 'arbiter/steward of their closeness to him'; 'steward' chosen for plain sense.
οὐ … πάντη τε καὶ πάντως: Cyril limits rather than flatly denies — not every child of the flesh is automatically a child of God; rendered 'would not, simply and in every case, be counted'.
ἐφ' ἑαυτοῖς τὴν ἐπὶ τῷδε δόξαν: 'the honor (glory) of this'; 'honor' chosen because δόξα here means standing or repute, not divine glory.
τῶν οὐ πάλαι διεγνωκότων: 'who had not known from ancient times', that is, latecomers to the knowledge of God.
